# Finding ∫ -3*x**4*sin(x) dx

I'll use the **tabular method** (repeated integration by parts):

| Differentiate | Integrate | Sign |
|---|---|---|
| -3*x**4 | -cos(x) | + |
| -12*x**3 | -sin(x) | − |
| -36*x**2 | cos(x) | + |
| -72*x | sin(x) | − |
| -72 | -cos(x) | + |

**Multiplying diagonally with alternating signs:**

$$= (+)(-3x^4)(-\cos x) + (-)(-12x^3)(-\sin x) + (+)(-36x^2)(\cos x) + (-)(-72x)(\sin x) + (+)(-72)(-\cos x)$$

**Simplifying each term:**

- $3x^4\cos(x)$
- $-12x^3\sin(x)$
- $-36x^2\cos(x)$
- $+72x\sin(x)$
- $+72\cos(x)$

**Verification** — differentiating the result gives back $-3x^4\sin(x)$ ✓ (all intermediate terms cancel).

<answer>3*x**4*cos(x) - 12*x**3*sin(x) - 36*x**2*cos(x) + 72*x*sin(x) + 72*cos(x) + C</answer>
